instructions: Put the 2 lb brisket, the 1.5 lb meaty bones and the 1.5 lb marrow bones in a large stockpot, at least 8 quarts. Cover them with cold water and bring it to a boil over high.
Meanwhile, cut the 2 onions in half and cut the ginger in half lengthwise.

Heat a heavy skillet over high with no oil until it starts to smoke. Put the onions and ginger in cut side down and leave them for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're blackened. Turn them over and char the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, then move them to a plate.

Turn the skillet down to medium high. Add the 7 star anise, the 3 cinnamon sticks, the 3 cardamom pods, the 2 cloves and the 1 tbsp coriander seeds. Toast them for about 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until they smell fragrant. Tip them onto the plate with the onions.
Once the pot boils, let it boil for 5 minutes. Gray foam will rise to the top. Drain everything into a colander, rinse each bone and the brisket under the tap, and wipe the pot clean.

Pour 10 cups water into the clean pot and bring it to a boil. Add the bones, the brisket, the charred onions and ginger, the toasted spices, the 4 tsp sugar and the 2 tsp salt. The water should only just cover everything.
When it's back to a simmer, turn the heat down to low so it barely bubbles. Cover it and simmer for 3 hours.
Lift the brisket out onto a plate. It should be very tender. Leave the pot to simmer uncovered for another 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, put the 4 oz tenderloin in the freezer for 20 minutes, until it feels firm. Slice it across the grain as thin as you can and keep it in the fridge.
Rinse the 8 oz bean sprouts. Pick the leaves from the Thai basil and the cilantro. Cut the 2 limes into wedges and slice the 2 chilies. Set them all out on the table with the hoisin and sriracha.

Pour the soup through a sieve into a clean pot and throw away the bones and spices. You want about 7 cups. If you have more, boil it for a few minutes to bring it down. If you have less, top it up with water.
Stir the 2 tbsp fish sauce into the soup and keep it simmering.
Slice the brisket thin across the grain. You'll need 3 to 5 slices a bowl. The rest keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
Cook the 8 oz noodles the way the packet says. Drain them very well.
Taste the soup. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lime.

Bring the soup up to a full boil. Divide the noodles between 4 big bowls and lay the brisket slices and raw tenderloin on top. Ladle about 1 2/3 cups of the boiling soup into each bowl. The raw beef turns pink in under a minute.
Serve with the bean sprouts, herbs, lime wedges, chilies, hoisin and sriracha on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions blanch the bones first, char onion and ginger, toast whole spices dry, simmer for about 3 hours, season the strained broth with fish sauce, salt and sugar, and pour it boiling over noodles and raw sliced beef. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) uses brisket with meaty and marrow bones, simmers covered for 3 hours, pulls the brisket and then simmers the bones uncovered for another 40 minutes. Vicky Pham uses soup bones, neck bones and bone-in short rib, adds fennel seed and optional MSG, pulls the meat as soon as it's tender and skims the fat off the strained broth. This one follows the lead, scaled to 4 bowls.
